memory_update.text: Core direct-exposure universe for ai_cluster_networking_optics: NVDA, ANET, AVGO, MRVL, COHR.
The node maps to three public-market sublayers: full-stack AI networking platforms, Ethernet switching/switch ASICs, and high-speed optical interconnect components/modules.

Potential follow-up candidates excluded by the five-name cap include Lumentum, Astera Labs, Ciena, Cisco, Corning, Fabrinet, Credo Technology, Applied Optoelectronics, Viavi, Intel and Amphenol. These should be screened in later passes for lasers/EMLs, connectivity ICs, DCI, fiber, test equipment, contract manufacturing and copper interconnect exposure.
Need later falsification work on whether the AI cluster bottleneck remains compute/HBM/power rather than networking/optics, and whether optics suppliers face margin compression despite unit growth.
Add AVGO as a high-confidence direct candidate for AI networking switch ASICs, Ethernet NICs, PHYs and custom AI rack systems.
Add ANET as a high-confidence direct candidate for AI/cloud Ethernet switching platforms and network software.
Add MRVL as a high-confidence direct candidate for optical DSPs, coherent DCI, PAM4 interconnect and custom AI fabric silicon.
Add COHR as a high-confidence direct candidate for AI datacenter optical transceivers, lasers, InP/photonics components and 800G/1.6T ramps.
Add GLW as a second-order fiber/connectivity infrastructure candidate; AI-specific revenue and margin sensitivity still need verification.

Potential omitted candidates for a later pass: LITE for lasers/transceivers, FN for optical manufacturing/packaging, CIEN for DCI/coherent optical systems, KEYS/VIAV for network/optical test equipment, and smaller silicon-photonics names that may be below the preferred USD 1B market-cap threshold.
AVGO should remain a core AI networking candidate because its public disclosures explicitly tie growth to Ethernet AI switches and custom AI accelerators.
ANET is a clean public-market mapping for AI Ethernet systems and software; next pass should verify AI networking revenue and hyperscaler concentration.
COHR is a strong optical-layer candidate with direct 800G/1.6T, CPO, silicon photonics, and optical circuit switch exposure.
CRDO is a less obvious AI connectivity supplier through active electrical cables, SerDes, retimers/DSPs, and short-reach cluster interconnect exposure.
GLW should be tracked as an adjacent physical-connectivity chokepoint: fiber density, cables, connectors, and data-center optical infrastructure may become constrained as AI data centers scale.

Potential next-pass candidates not included due to the 5-name limit: MRVL for optical DSP/custom silicon/silicon photonics; LITE for EML lasers, pump lasers, 800G transceivers and CPO components; FN for outsourced optical manufacturing; CIEN for coherent DCI; NVDA for InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, NVLink and AI networking systems.

The strongest sub-nodes to track are: Ethernet switch ASICs, high-speed switching systems, 800G/1.6T optical transceivers, laser components, silicon photonics, active electrical cables, SerDes/DSPs, and high-density fiber/connectors.
